skill.name: slidev
skill.description: Create and present web-based slidedecks for developers using Slidev with Markdown, Vue components, code highlighting, animations, and interactive features. Use when building technical presentations, conference talks, code walkthroughs, teaching materials, or developer decks.
skill.summary: Build developer presentations in Slidev with Markdown, Vue, interactive code, diagrams, animations, presenter tools, and export guidance.
skill.author: antfu

security_audit.summary: Review found 105 static alerts, predominantly false positives caused by Markdown backticks, example URLs, Mermaid terminology, and local screen-recording documentation. PlantUML configuration can send diagram source to a remote server, and remote presenter mode can expose a network control surface. No prompt injection, covert upload, credential access, or malicious command construction was found.

remediation.issue: Remote presenter mode creates a network-accessible control surface.
remediation.suggestion: Document password protection, trusted-network binding, and explicit approval before enabling remote access or a public tunnel.

remediation.issue: PlantUML rendering can send diagram source to an external server.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users before remote rendering and recommend a trusted self-hosted server for confidential diagrams.

content.user_title: Build Interactive Developer Slides with Slidev
content.value_statement: Technical presentations often require code, diagrams, animation, and reliable export workflows. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Slidev syntax and tooling.
actual_capabilities: Creates Slidev deck structures with headmatter, frontmatter, slide separators, and presenter notes.
Applies built-in layouts, named slots, scoped styles, global layers, and draggable elements.
Adds highlighted code, line transitions, code groups, Monaco editors, and imported snippets.
Adds Mermaid, PlantUML, and LaTeX content using documented Slidev syntax.
Configures click animations, drawings, timers, recording, and presenter controls.
Guides local preview, static builds, PDF or PPTX export, hosting, and SEO metadata.
limitations: It does not include Slidev, Node.js, package managers, browsers, themes, or export dependencies.
Remote assets, PlantUML rendering, themes, and package installation can require network access.
Recording requires explicit camera or screen permission and compatible browser support.
Export quality and supported formats depend on the installed Slidev and browser versions.

best_practices: Keep one main idea per slide and use presenter notes for supporting detail.
Use progressive highlighting and click reveals only when sequence improves understanding.
Test local preview, fonts, remote assets, code overflow, and export output before delivery.
anti_patterns: Do not place long source files or dense paragraphs on a single slide.
Do not enable recording or remote presenter access without explicit user approval.
Do not send confidential diagrams or assets to untrusted remote services.

faq.question: Does this skill install Slidev?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and can prepare project content, but Slidev and its dependencies must be available in the target environment.

faq.question: Can it create PDF or PPTX exports?
faq.answer: It can configure and guide export workflows. Actual export requires Slidev, a compatible browser dependency, and a working local environment.

faq.question: Does it support Vue components?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers built-in components, custom Vue usage, layouts, slots, global layers, and lifecycle hooks.

faq.question: Can it add interactive code examples?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents Monaco editing, runnable examples, code groups, imported snippets, highlighting, and animated code transitions.

faq.question: Does recording upload my camera or screen?
faq.answer: The referenced workflow records with browser APIs and saves WebM output. Users must still review browser permissions and storage behavior.

faq.question: Can the deck work offline?
faq.answer: Yes, when themes, fonts, diagrams, and assets are local or cached. Remote services must be replaced or prepared before offline use.
